```{r}
library(tidyverse)

library(broom)
library(psych)

library(apa)
```

```{r}
# Import coding

# Exp 2

raw_video_coding_henry_exp2 <- read_csv(here::here("data", "disagreement_exp2_video_coding_2.csv"),
                                          skip = 2) %>%
  select(-`Going in to the interaction, to what extent do you think these participants agreed versus disagreed on the topic?\n(Type number only, from -5 = strongly disagree initially to 5 = strongly agree initially)`) %>%
  # It looks like Henry added an extra row for video 98
  filter(`Video Number \n` != 98)

raw_video_coding_akshaj_exp2 <- read_csv(here::here("data", "disagreement_exp2_video_coding_1.csv"),
                                          skip = 2) %>%
  select(-`Going in to the interaction, to what extent do you think these participants agreed versus disagreed on the topic?\n(Type number only, from -5 = strongly disagree initially to 5 = strongly agree initially)`)


# Exp 3

raw_video_coding_joan_exp4 <- read_csv(here::here("data", "disagreement_exp3_video_coding_1.csv"),
                                          skip = 3) %>%
  select(-`Going in to the interaction, to what extent do you think these participants agreed versus disagreed on the topic?\n(Type number only, from -5 = strongly disagree initially to 5 = strongly agree initially)`)

raw_video_coding_evalise_exp4 <- read_csv(here::here("data", "disagreement_exp3_video_coding_2.csv"),
                                          skip = 3) %>%
  select(-`Going in to the interaction, to what extent do you think these participants agreed versus disagreed on the topic?\n(Type number only, from -5 = strongly disagree initially to 5 = strongly agree initially)`)

# Import cleaned datasets from the original experiments, selecting the key variables
exp2_original_data <- read_csv(here::here("data", "disagreement_exp2_cleaned_data.csv")) %>%
  dplyr::select(PairID, Condition, ConditionCombined, Enjoy, Hostile)

exp4_original_data <- read_csv(here::here("data", "disagreement_exp3_cleaned_data.csv")) %>%
  dplyr::select(session_number, agree_condition, mode_condition, enjoy, hostile)
# Note that we were originally calling Experiment 3 "experiment 4," hence the labels here and throughout
  
```

```{r}
# Rename columns with shorter names

# Henry
henry_coding <- raw_video_coding_henry_exp2 %>%
  rename(session_number = `Video Number \n`,
         topic = `Topic Discussed (copy and paste "Label" from Discussion Topics tab)`,
         minutes_on = `Total Number of Minutes Spent ON Topic\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)`,
         total_minutes = `Total Number of Minutes Spent Discussing\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)\nOnly time spent actually discussing should be counted here (but this includes both time ON topic and time OFF topic)`,
         express_agree = `To what extent did the participants express AGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         express_disagree = `To what extent did the participants express DISAGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         predicted_condition = `Which condition do you think participants were in? \n(Type "Agree," "Disagree")`,
         enjoy = `How much did the participants seem to enjoy the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = a lot)`,
         hostile = `How much hostility was expressed during the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = very)`,
         notes = `(Optional) Any notes about this session? (E.g., did anything weird happen? Was there a big discrepancy in how much each participant seemed to enjoy the interaction? Anything else noteworthy?)`) %>%
    # Changing format of time variable "minutes on." Note that R thinks the minutes are hours and the seconds are minutes.
  mutate(minutes_only_on = hour(minutes_on),
         seconds_only_on = minute(minutes_on),
         time_fraction_on = minutes_only_on + (seconds_only_on / 60),
         total_minutes_only = hour(total_minutes),
         total_seconds_only = minute(total_minutes),
         total_time_fraction = total_minutes_only + (total_seconds_only / 60),
         predicted_condition = tolower(predicted_condition)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(minutes_on)) 

# Akshahj
akshaj_coding <- raw_video_coding_akshaj_exp2 %>%
  rename(session_number = `Video Number \n`,
         topic = `Topic Discussed (copy and paste "Label" from Discussion Topics tab)`,
         minutes_on = `Total Number of Minutes Spent ON Topic\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)`,
         total_minutes = `Total Number of Minutes Spent Discussing\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)\nOnly time spent actually discussing should be counted here (but this includes both time ON topic and time OFF topic)`,
         express_agree = `To what extent did the participants express AGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         express_disagree = `To what extent did the participants express DISAGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         predicted_condition = `Which condition do you think participants were in? \n(Type "Agree," "Disagree")`,
         enjoy = `How much did the participants seem to enjoy the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = a lot)`,
         hostile = `How much hostility was expressed during the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = very)`,
         notes = `(Optional) Any notes about this session? (E.g., did anything weird happen? Was there a big discrepancy in how much each participant seemed to enjoy the interaction? Anything else noteworthy?)`) %>%
    # Changing format of time variable "minutes on." Note that R thinks the minutes are hours and the seconds are minutes.
  mutate(minutes_only_on = hour(minutes_on),
         seconds_only_on = minute(minutes_on),
         time_fraction_on = minutes_only_on + (seconds_only_on / 60),
         total_minutes_only = hour(total_minutes),
         total_seconds_only = minute(total_minutes),
         total_time_fraction = total_minutes_only + (total_seconds_only / 60),
         predicted_condition = tolower(predicted_condition)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(minutes_on)) 

# Joan
joan_coding <- raw_video_coding_joan_exp4 %>%
  rename(session_number = `Video Number \n`,
         topic = `Topic Discussed (copy and paste "Label" from Discussion Topics tab)`,
         minutes_on = `Total Number of Minutes Spent ON Topic\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)`,
         total_minutes = `Total Number of Minutes Spent Discussing\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)\nOnly time spent actually discussing should be counted here (but this includes both time ON topic and time OFF topic)`,
         express_agree = `To what extent did the participants express AGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         express_disagree = `To what extent did the participants express DISAGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         predicted_condition = `Which condition do you think participants were in? \n(Type "Agree," "Disagree")`,
         enjoy = `How much did the participants seem to enjoy the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = a lot)`,
         hostile = `How much hostility was expressed during the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = very)`,
         notes = `(Optional) Any notes about this session? (E.g., did anything weird happen? Was there a big discrepancy in how much each participant seemed to enjoy the interaction? Anything else noteworthy?)`) %>%
    # Changing format of time variable "minutes on." Note that R thinks the minutes are hours and the seconds are minutes.
  mutate(minutes_only_on = hour(minutes_on),
         seconds_only_on = minute(minutes_on),
         time_fraction_on = minutes_only_on + (seconds_only_on / 60),
         total_minutes_only = hour(total_minutes),
         total_seconds_only = minute(total_minutes),
         total_time_fraction = total_minutes_only + (total_seconds_only / 60),
         predicted_condition = tolower(predicted_condition)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(minutes_on)) %>%
  # Exclude sessions where P's discussed different topics or there was a video from the wrong study in the pair (both in the monologue condition)
  filter(session_number != 100, session_number != 104)

# Evalise
evalise_coding <- raw_video_coding_evalise_exp4 %>%
  rename(session_number = `Video Number \n`,
         topic = `Topic Discussed (copy and paste "Label" from Discussion Topics tab)`,
         minutes_on = `Total Number of Minutes Spent ON Topic\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)`,
         total_minutes = `Total Number of Minutes Spent Discussing\n(Type in the following format: min:sec (e.g., 6:50, 4:33, etc.); add the sum of the two videos if in monologue condition)\nOnly time spent actually discussing should be counted here (but this includes both time ON topic and time OFF topic)`,
         express_agree = `To what extent did the participants express AGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         express_disagree = `To what extent did the participants express DISAGREEING with each other in this interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = none at all to 5 = complete agreement)`,
         predicted_condition = `Which condition do you think participants were in? \n(Type "Agree," "Disagree")`,
         enjoy = `How much did the participants seem to enjoy the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = a lot)`,
         hostile = `How much hostility was expressed during the interaction?\n(Type number only, from 0 = not at all to 10 = very)`,
         notes = `(Optional) Any notes about this session? (E.g., did anything weird happen? Was there a big discrepancy in how much each participant seemed to enjoy the interaction? Anything else noteworthy?)`) %>%
    # Changing format of time variable "minutes on." Note that R thinks the minutes are hours and the seconds are minutes.
  mutate(minutes_only_on = hour(minutes_on),
         seconds_only_on = minute(minutes_on),
         time_fraction_on = minutes_only_on + (seconds_only_on / 60),
         total_minutes_only = hour(total_minutes),
         total_seconds_only = minute(total_minutes),
         total_time_fraction = total_minutes_only + (total_seconds_only / 60),
         predicted_condition = tolower(predicted_condition)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(minutes_on)) %>%
  # Exclude sessions where P's discussed different topics or there was a video from the wrong study in the pair (both in the monologue condition)
  filter(session_number != 100, session_number != 104) %>%
  # Convert some numbers treated as characters into numberics
  mutate(express_agree = as.numeric(express_agree),
         express_disagree = as.numeric(express_disagree),
         enjoy = as.numeric(enjoy))
```


```{r}
# For original datasets, filter to one observation per session, so that can compare the conditions

exp2_data_session_level <- exp2_original_data %>%
  distinct(PairID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  # rename Pair ID column so name is consistent with coding file, and also get rid of the letters so that it's just the session numbers (so can match)
  mutate(session_number = as.numeric(stringr::str_remove_all(PairID, "[A-Z]"))) %>%
  mutate(agree_condition = fct_recode(factor(Condition),
                                      "agree" = "1",
                                      "disagree" = "2",
                                      "agree" = "4",
                                      "disagree" = "5"))

exp4_data_session_level <- exp4_original_data %>%
  distinct(session_number, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Create combined datasets (with original data) matched by session numbers - this data is session level, for condition predictions

# Exp 2

# Henry
combined_exp2_henry <- left_join(henry_coding, exp2_data_session_level, by = "session_number") %>%
  # Get rid of the subjective variables because they are not meaningful here (they are only from one participant, not an average of both)
  dplyr::select(-Enjoy, -Hostile) %>%
  mutate(correct_prediction = 0)

# Create function for saying if condition prediction is correct or not
for(i in seq_along(combined_exp2_henry$correct_prediction)) {
  if(combined_exp2_henry$predicted_condition[i] == combined_exp2_henry$agree_condition[i]) {
    combined_exp2_henry$correct_prediction[i] = 1
  } else {
    combined_exp2_henry$correct_prediction[i] = 0
  }
}

# Akshaj
combined_exp2_akshaj <- left_join(akshaj_coding, exp2_data_session_level, by = "session_number") %>%
  # Get rid of the subjective variables because they are not meaningful here (they are only from one participant, not an average of both)
  dplyr::select(-Enjoy, -Hostile) %>%
  mutate(correct_prediction = 0)

# Create function for saying if condition prediction is correct or not
for(i in seq_along(combined_exp2_akshaj$correct_prediction)) {
  if(combined_exp2_akshaj$predicted_condition[i] == combined_exp2_akshaj$agree_condition[i]) {
    combined_exp2_akshaj$correct_prediction[i] = 1
  } else {
    combined_exp2_akshaj$correct_prediction[i] = 0
  }
}

# Exp 3

# Joan
combined_exp4_joan <- left_join(joan_coding, exp4_data_session_level, by = "session_number") %>%
  # Get rid of the subjective variables because they are not meaningful here (they are only from one participant, not an average of both)
  dplyr::select(-enjoy.y, -hostile.y) %>%
  rename(enjoy = enjoy.x,
         hostile = hostile.x) %>%
  mutate(correct_prediction = 0)

# Create function for saying if condition prediction is correct or not
for(i in seq_along(combined_exp4_joan$correct_prediction)) {
  if(combined_exp4_joan$predicted_condition[i] == combined_exp4_joan$agree_condition[i]) {
    combined_exp4_joan$correct_prediction[i] = 1
  } else {
    combined_exp4_joan$correct_prediction[i] = 0
  }
}

# Evalise
combined_exp4_evalise <- left_join(evalise_coding, exp4_data_session_level, by = "session_number") %>%
  # Get rid of the subjective variables because they are not meaningful here (they are only from one participant, not an average of both)
  dplyr::select(-enjoy.y, -hostile.y) %>%
    rename(enjoy = enjoy.x,
         hostile = hostile.x) %>%
  mutate(correct_prediction = 0)

# Create function for saying if condition prediction is correct or not
for(i in seq_along(combined_exp4_evalise$correct_prediction)) {
  if(combined_exp4_evalise$predicted_condition[i] == combined_exp4_evalise$agree_condition[i]) {
    combined_exp4_evalise$correct_prediction[i] = 1
  } else {
    combined_exp4_evalise$correct_prediction[i] = 0
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Combine coder datasets together and take average of ratings
# Exp 2
exp2_averaged_data <- inner_join(combined_exp2_henry, combined_exp2_akshaj, by = "session_number") %>%
  # The condition column gets duplicated when combine, so will remove one and rename the other (below)
  select(-agree_condition.y) %>%
  mutate(avg_time_fraction_on = (time_fraction_on.x + time_fraction_on.y) / 2,
         avg_total_time_fraction = (total_time_fraction.x + total_time_fraction.y) / 2,
         avg_express_agree = (express_agree.x + express_agree.y) / 2,
         avg_express_disagree = (express_disagree.x + express_disagree.y) / 2,
         avg_enjoy = (enjoy.x + enjoy.y) / 2,
         avg_hostile = (hostile.x + hostile.y) / 2) %>%
  rename(agree_condition = agree_condition.x)

exp4_averaged_data <- inner_join(combined_exp4_joan, combined_exp4_evalise, by = "session_number") %>%
  select(-agree_condition.y, -mode_condition.y) %>%
  mutate(avg_time_fraction_on = (time_fraction_on.x + time_fraction_on.y) / 2,
         avg_total_time_fraction = (total_time_fraction.x + total_time_fraction.y) / 2,
         avg_express_agree = (express_agree.x + express_agree.y) / 2,
         avg_express_disagree = (express_disagree.x + express_disagree.y) / 2,
         avg_enjoy = (enjoy.x + enjoy.y) / 2,
         avg_hostile = (hostile.x + hostile.y) / 2) %>%
  rename(agree_condition = agree_condition.x,
         mode_condition = mode_condition.x)
```

# Main Analyses: Averaged Ratings by Conditions

## Experiment 2

```{r}
exp2_averaged_data %>%
  group_by(agree_condition) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(avg_time_fraction_on),
            sd = sd(avg_time_fraction_on)) 
```

```{r}
wrap.t.ind(exp2_averaged_data$avg_time_fraction_on, factor(exp2_averaged_data$agree_condition))
```

## Experiment 4

**Time On Topic**

```{r}
exp4_averaged_data %>%
  group_by(agree_condition, mode_condition) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(avg_time_fraction_on),
            sd = sd(avg_time_fraction_on))
```

```{r}
time_on_anova <- aov_car(avg_time_fraction_on ~ agree_condition * mode_condition + Error(session_number),
                         data = exp4_averaged_data,  type = "III", 
                            anova_table = list(es = "pes"), include_aov = TRUE)
anova_apa(time_on_anova , print = FALSE) %>%
  kable(caption = "ANOVA")
```

```{r}
pairs(emmeans(time_on_anova, "agree_condition", by = c("mode_condition"))) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans(time_on_anova, ~ agree_condition * mode_condition))) %>%
  arrange(p.value)
```

# Supplemental Analyses: Agreement Between Coders & Accuracy

## Experiment 2

**Time On Topic**

Correlation:

```{r}
#cor(henry_coding$time_fraction_on, akshaj_coding$time_fraction_on)
cor_apa(cor.test(henry_coding$time_fraction_on, akshaj_coding$time_fraction_on))
```

Average rating difference:

*Written in fractions of a minute*

```{r}
mean(henry_coding$time_fraction_on - akshaj_coding$time_fraction_on)
```


\newpage

**Total Time Discussing**

Correlation:

```{r}
cor_apa(cor.test(henry_coding$total_time_fraction, akshaj_coding$total_time_fraction))
```

*This low correlation is surely because there is very little variance - conversations were fixed at 10 min.*

Average rating difference:

*Written in fractions of a minute*

```{r}
mean(henry_coding$total_time_fraction - akshaj_coding$total_time_fraction)
```

\newpage
